taps.phrase: to jump high into the sky

story: Our boat races a dolphin across the blue sea.
The dolphin jumps high into the sky and lands with a splash!
It wins the race, and it doesn't even have a motor!
notes: A59 rewrite (owner rule 1 + owner request to drop the weak nouns sea / water / air, sea and water being the same surface). Phrase 1 now holds the key word: 'to race a dolphin', doer = the boat the clip is filmed from (its chrome railing is clearly in the picture 0-3 s while the dolphin swims fast alongside, then the dolphin races ahead); own boxes on the railing 0-3 s, off from 3.5 s; the boxes stay below the dolphin's live region at every key time. Phrases 2 and 3 keep the dolphin (live:1 region) with new, clearly separate nouns: the sky (top of the still) and a splash (the white splash under the leaping dolphin in the still; it lands with splashes at 6.5 s and 9.5 s). Nouns: a dolphin on the leaping dolphin, sky top-left, a splash on the white splash. Gaps: race (verb), the sky (noun), land with (verb); bank pieces all different from the partners pod of / swim with / feed. Story rewritten around the race; phrase 1 inflected in sentence 1. Exercise 1 now shown (two targets, no cut), but the boat is visible only 0-3 s; tiny far dolphins on the horizon at 8-10 s also jump but are specks.
